**SEC. 525 – Honorary Space Force Designation for Separated Air Force Members**
- Adds new §9254 to Chapter 933, Title 10, U.S. Code.
- Secretary of the Air Force may prescribe regulations designating eligible individuals as "honorary separated members of the Space Force" ("Legacy Guardian").
- Eligible individual: determined by SecAF to have served in support of space operations as an Air Force member, and who separated (or previously separated) as an Air Force member.
- Regulations may include: eligibility criteria (dates of service, constructive service credit), application process (by individual or survivor of deceased individual), and certificate/insignia.
- Designation confers no additional benefits beyond those established by the section or its regulations.

**SEC. 526 – Medal of Honor and Distinguished Service Cross Authorizations**
- (a) President may posthumously award Medal of Honor to Roderick W. Edmonds (Master Sergeant, Army) for actions Jan 27–Mar 30, 1945. Waives time limitations in 10 U.S.C. §7274 and any other time limitation. Award under §7271.
- (b) President may posthumously award Distinguished Service Cross to William D. Owens (Staff Sergeant, Army) for actions Jun 6–8, 1944, at La Fiere Bridge (previously awarded Bronze Star). Same time-limit waivers. Award under §7272.

**SEC. 527 – Posthumous Advancement of General John D. Lavelle**
- General John D. Lavelle (USAF, retired) entitled to hold rank of lieutenant general on the Air Force retired list.
- No additional retired pay or other benefits accrue from the advancement; benefits to other persons unaffected.

## SEC. 924 — Office of Expanded Competition
- **Purpose:** Establishes Office of Expanded Competition in Office of Secretary of Air Force.
- **Mechanism:** Adds new §9025 to Chapter 903, Title 10 USC.
- **Director:** Appointed by SecAF from DoD employees who are either in SES position at appointment or meet ECQs.
- **Duties (9 listed):** Assess adversarial capital flows; identify/prioritize critical technologies/assets needing capital assistance; fund investments; support coordination/outreach for technology scouting; identify/accelerate tangible/intangible asset establishment; provide capital assistance (incl. foreign entities); experiment/prototype analytical tools; assist SecDef in commercial access/placement; coordinate across DoD/Federal Government.
- **Definitions:** "Adversarial capital flow" = investment by government of adversary country or entity organized under laws of/subject to jurisdiction of such country. "Capital assistance" = loan, loan guarantee, or technical assistance.
- **Briefing deadline:** SecAF briefs congressional defense committees ≤180 days after enactment on implementation status.

## SEC. 925 — Counter Unmanned Aerial Systems Task Force
- **Establishment:** SecDef establishes/designates C-UAS Task Force ≤30 days after enactment.
- **Review of memoranda/directives:** SecDef and CJCS, through Task Force, review and consolidate/update all DoD memoranda/directives re: countering UAS in US airspace ≤90 days after enactment. Specific documents listed (A–G).
- **Issuance of updated guidance:** SecDef issues new memoranda/directives/guidance ≤120 days after enactment.
- **Dissemination:** Included in pre-briefings for officers assuming command of military installations in US on/after July 1, 2025.
- **Standard operating procedures:** Each installation commander issues SOPs ≤60 days after issuance of updated guidance. If change of command during 60-day period, incoming commander issues SOPs ≤60 days after pre-briefing.
- **Report on training efforts:** SecDef submits report to congressional defense committees ≤120 days after enactment on C-UAS training efforts, including commonly provided training and curriculum summary for installation commanders/deployed forces.

## SEC. 926 — Affiliate Relationships Between Army SOF and Combat-Enabling Units of GPF
- **Limitation:** No FY2025 funds may be obligated/expended to complete SOF structure reductions described in subsection (b) until assessment under subsection (c) submitted.
- **Reductions described:** Proposed reductions to end strengths of Army SOF announced February 27, 2024, as part of Total Army Analysis process.
- **Assessment:** SecArmy and ASD(SOLIC) jointly submit report ≤180 days after enactment assessing feasibility/advisability of formal affiliate relationships between Army SOF units and Army GPF combat-enabling units (logistics, intelligence, communications, EOD, electronic warfare, rotary wing, combat medicine, info ops, civil affairs, others).
- **Considerations:** Enabling requirements; availability of high-demand, low-density capabilities; deployment-to-dwell standards; ability to fulfill service-specific and joint force requirements.
- **Plan:** If feasible/advisable, SecArmy and ASD(SOLIC) jointly submit plan ≤270 days after enactment, including unit identification and timeline.
- **Definitions:** "Affiliate relationship" = habitual relationship where units regularly train, exercise, and deploy together. "Special operations forces" = forces identified under 10 USC §167(j). "Special operations activities" = activities described in 10 USC §167(k).

## SEC. 927 — Force Sizing Methodology
- **Methodology development:** SecDef develops methodology ≤180 days after enactment for analyzing US military force sizing for activities below threshold of traditional armed conflict (campaigning, security cooperation, info ops, civil affairs, irregular warfare, operational preparation of environment).
- **Report:** SecDef submits report ≤270 days after enactment, including methodology explanation, roles/responsibilities, other relevant matters.

## SEC. 1001 — General Transfer Authority
- **Authority:** SecDef may transfer authorizations between DoD accounts for FY2025 upon determination of national interest.
- **Limitation:** Total transfers may not exceed $6,000,000,000.
- **Exception:** Transfers between military personnel authorizations under Title IV not counted toward dollar limitation.
- **Conditions:** Transfers only for higher-priority items; may not fund items denied authorization by Congress.
- **Notice:** SecDef promptly notifies Congress of each transfer.

- **Deadline:** Not later than 180 days after enactment, and annually thereafter for three years.

- **Contract requirement:** Not later than 60 days after enactment, Secretary of Defense shall seek to contract with an FFRDC (or FFRDC + private management consulting team), not sponsored by Army or Navy, to review construction project roles/responsibilities.
- **Report deadline:** Not later than February 1, 2026, submitted to SASC and HASC.
- **18 enumerated assessment elements** covering: design/construction delivery processes of Army Corps of Engineers and Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC); workforce counts by specialty; workforce adequacy; internal controls and financial processes; real estate functions; geographic regions; construction performance measures; infrastructure requirement generation and cost estimation; Army Corps non-construction-agent capabilities; Navy use of NAVFAC for other functions; Army/Air Force FSRM design/construction; data/software systems; organizational alignment of authorities; potential cost savings/performance improvements from single construction agent; existing efficiencies; alternatives for single construction agent alignment; cost assessment including redundant costs and personnel estimates.
- **Briefings:** Initial briefing not later than 30 days after contract execution (including estimated timeline); quarterly briefings thereafter to SASC and HASC.

**SEC. 2878. Assessment of Public Schools on DoD Installations**
- **Updated assessment:** Not later than one year after enactment, Secretary of Defense shall submit to congressional defense committees an updated assessment of capacity and facility condition deficiencies of elementary/secondary public schools on military installations (updating July 2011 assessment under §8109 of Public Law 112-10, as updated July 2017 under §2814 of Public Law 114-328).

*Subtitle A — Foundation (secs. 5102–5109)*
- Board members serve without pay; reimbursed for actual/necessary travel. Overseas reimbursement requires ≥2 Board members traveling concurrently; limited to published per diem; no first/business-class travel.
- Board members are not federal employees.
- Board removal: appointed member missing 3 consecutive meetings may be removed by majority Board vote.
- Board duties: establish bylaws, direct activities, evaluate Executive Director, limit admin expenses, annually consult stakeholders on protected/conserved area management.
- Bylaws must include: Executive Director duties; selection policies; ethical standards for donations/grants and dissolution asset disposition; conflict-of-interest standards for all agents; removal/exclusion procedures; wind-down plan (return unspent appropriations to Treasury; donate unspent private/philanthropic contributions per sec. 5106 goals); vetting policies to bar for-profit non-conservation entities; clawback provisions.
- Foundation staff: may not be U.S. Government employees; may not work for grantees; may not receive outside compensation; salary capped at Exec Schedule Level I (5 U.S.C. 5312).

Foundation may not support individuals/entities tied to current or former Board members (5-year post-term bar).

# Working Notes — Part 21/21, Division G (Department of State Authorization Act, FY2025)

## SEC. 7215 — Rest & Recuperation / Overseas Operations Leave
- **Amends:** Foreign Service Act of 1980, Chapter 9 (22 U.S.C. 4081 et seq.) — inserts new §§903a and 903b after §903 (22 U.S.C. 4083).
- **§903a (22 U.S.C. 4083a) — R&R Leave:** Agency heads may prescribe regs granting up to **20 days paid leave per leave year** to employees serving in combat zones, high-risk/high-threat posts, or locations with significant security/operational challenges. Sole discretion of agency head. Leave recorded separately from other leave.
- **§903b (22 U.S.C. 4083b) — Overseas Operations Leave:** Agency heads may prescribe regs granting up to **10 days paid leave per leave year** to employees serving abroad for local holidays. Sole discretion of agency head.
- **Definitions:** "Agency" = Executive agency (5 U.S.C. §105), excluding GAO. "Employee" excludes uniformed services. "Combat zone" includes DoD-certified combat zone tax benefit locations. "High risk, high threat post" per 22 U.S.C. §4803. "Leave year" = first complete pay period start to day before next year's.
- **Clerical amendment:** Updates table of contents of Foreign Service Act of 1980.

## SEC. 7216 — Overseas Crisis Response System and Strategy (22 U.S.C. 4865 note)
- **Senior Focal Point:** Secretary designates senior official for crisis management/response; reports directly to Secretary. Duties: coordinate crisis response, liaise with USAID/regional bureaus, facilitate after-action reviews, maintain congressional liaison.
- **Tabletop exercises:** Within **120 days** of enactment, and annually for **3 years**. Address crisis response/evacuation requirements including leadership roles, structures, drawdown/evacuation processes, and assistance to private US citizens, USG employees/dependents, allies, local nationals, third-country nationals. May consult DoD, other agencies, State/local governments; may invite foreign allies, NGOs.
- **Briefing:** Within **90 days** after each exercise, brief appropriate congressional committees + SASC/HASC. May be classified. After **3 years** post-enactment, written notice replaces briefing.
- **FSI training:** Review crisis management curricula; ambassadorial seminar and DCM course must include crisis management curriculum (town halls, high-threat communications, drawdown/evacuation, citizen assistance, tabletop exercises, locally employed staff needs).
- **Clearinghouse:** Within **180 days**, establish "Department of State Emergency Response Lessons Learned Clearinghouse" — central electronic repository of lessons learned/after-action reports.
- **"International crisis" defined:** Any overseas situation requiring change in operating status of US diplomatic facilities (diplomatic post-led/military-assisted departure, ordered departure, noncombatant evacuation).

## SEC. 7301 — Regional Technology Officer Program
- **Amends:** §9508(a)(1) of Department of State Authorizations Act of 2022 (22 U.S.C. 10305(a)(1)) — adds administration by Bureau for Cyberspace and Digital Policy.

## SEC. 7302 — Protecting Department Devices from Foreign Commercial Spyware (22 U.S.C. 10308 note)
- **Definitions:** "Covered device" = Department-issued mobile electronic devices. "Foreign commercial spyware"/"spyware" per 50 U.S.C. §3232a.
- **Within 120 days:** Secretary issues standards/guidance/policies; surveys compromises over prior **2 years**; reports to appropriate congressional committees (may be classified).
- **Notifications:** Within **60 days** of awareness of serious compromise, notify committees with location, number of devices, damage assessment, and assessment of responsible foreign actors.
- **Annual report:** Within **1 year** of enactment, and annually for **5 years**, report to committees including Senate/House Judiciary.

## SEC. 7303 — Cloud Computing in Bureau of Consular Affairs
- Within **90 days**, Secretary reports to appropriate congressional committees on cloud adoption status and enterprise-wide options.

## SEC. 7304 — IT Pilot Projects
- Within **180 days**, CIO (consulting with Assistant Secretary of Consular Affairs) should consider piloting **≥3 IT systems** prioritizing passport renewal acceleration and legacy system reduction.

## SEC. 7305 — Leveraging Technology for Administrative Efficiencies (22 U.S.C. 2651a note)
- Secretary and Administrator ensure appropriate/secure technological solutions authorized and available for employee use, including secure tools in performance evaluation.

## SEC. 7401 — US Agency for Global Media
- **Amends:** §306 of US International Broadcasting Act of 1994 (22 U.S.C. §6205). Redesignates subsections (f)→(g), (g)→(h). New subsection (f): Grantee suspension/debarment requires CEO consultation and **three-fourths majority vote** of Advisory Board. Suspension criteria per 22 C.F.R. §513.405; Advisory Board collectively serves as suspending official (22 C.F.R. §513.105). Debarment criteria per 22 C.F.R.
